The inspected lesson data and bundle bind the S.1 ID/text to the expected S.1 file; the static invocation requests one S.1 line. No extra T clip is specified there.
The old continuous SSML request contains only L/I/M/A phoneme tags and breaks, with no requested T.
Unprimed English Scribe v2 transcribed the actual old S.1 as L-I-M say A, while the separate current sources returned L, I, M, A.
New S.1 is derived from complete current canonical waveforms with explicit digital silence and no sequence synthesis. Each source and its exact frame interval is recorded.
hypotheses: An unwanted acoustic transition in the continuous generation is the leading explanation consistent with the user report and directed ASR; its precise phonetic or internal model cause has not been established.
limitations: ASR does not establish that the unwanted sound is exactly /t/, and isolated-letter recognition is not perfect phonetic proof.
Read-only file and bundle tracing does not prove the exact browser/cache/runtime state of the user session. No browser runtime QA was performed.
Signal-envelope metrics locate energy only and do not identify phonemes.
The new assembled S.1 and afternoon were not played or transcribed; final perceptual review belongs to the user.
Deterministic composition prevents new sequence-TTS transitions; it does not guarantee the perceptual correctness of each pre-existing source.
